section_summary.extract_value: The Discussion summarizes a single study investigating how self-compassionate engagement and action, and psychological flexibility/inflexibility, relate to body appreciation in adult women. It reports that psychological flexibility (lower psychological inflexibility) and self-compassionate action directly predict body appreciation, that self-compassionate engagement relates indirectly via these mechanisms, and it notes methodological limitations including cross-sectional design, snowball sampling, and use of a confidential web survey.
section_summary.evidence_source: "the main aim of the present study was to explore the role of general psychological flexibility...and how these mechanisms may associate with higher body appreciation on adult women." Also: "the used survey web app is completely confidential..." and "the use of the Exponential Non-Discriminative Snowball Sampling method (Heckathorn, 2011)".

section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion summarizes findings from the present (single) study examining how self-compassionate engagement, self-compassionate action, and psychological inflexibility relate to body appreciation in adult women. A path analysis (see Fig. 1) found that self-compassionate action and lower psychological inflexibility directly predict higher body appreciation, and that psychological inflexibility mediates the link between engagement and action.
section_summary.evidence_source: "the main aim of the present study was to explore..."; "Results revealed that among emotion regulation, only self-compassionate action and psychological inflexibility act as direct predictors of an accepting and protective attitude toward body image."; Fig. 1 (final path model).
